motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Marian Burningham as a Community Services Board Member from April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Marian Burningham joins Community Services Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Marian Burningham to the Community Services Board for a term running April 2026 through March 2029.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 14.A. and 14.B. and moving them to Scheduled Items. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed by a vote of 4:0, with one abstention.
motions.headline: Routine items grouped; two land items pulled out
motions.summary: The council took up its batch of routine consent items, pulling the two Overland land agreements out to be handled separately.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the housekeeping step that clears routine items in one vote and moves the two land items into open discussion.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area conditioned upon : 1. Reciprocal language be added to Section 8 of the agreement ; and 2. SITLA guarantees clean title of warranty . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land swap with the state in the Overland area
motions.summary: The city approved trading properties with the state trust lands agency (SITLA) in the Overland area, conditioned on matching contract language and a clean title guarantee.
motions.impact: It reshuffles which parcels the city and the state each own out in the Overland area. Nothing changes at your home now, but it shapes what the city can do with that land later.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Memorandum of Agreement Concerning Overland.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Memorandum of Agreement Concerning Overland. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Agreement approved over the Overland area
motions.summary: The council approved a memorandum of agreement concerning Overland; the motion itself does not spell out the terms.
motions.impact: The record gives no detail on what the city agreed to, so no effect on residents can honestly be described. It was pulled off the consent agenda for separate discussion.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Portion of Utah Cou nty Parcel #46:489:0159 of Designated “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal : 1. The purchase price for the property is established at $2.07 per square foot, with the total amount determined by the final surveyed areas ; and 2. All existing utility easements on the property shall be maintained
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Portion of Utah Cou nty Parcel #46:489:0159 of Designated “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal : 1. The purchase price for the property is established at $2.07 per square foot, with the total amount determined by the final surveyed areas ; and 2. All existing utility easements on the property shall be maintained . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to sell land at $2.07 a square foot
motions.summary: The council approved selling part of a city-owned parcel at $2.07 per square foot, with the total set by the final survey.
motions.impact: This is a one-off sale of city land and changes nothing at your home. Existing utility easements on the property stay in place, so the lines running through it are protected.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan , directing consultant to take feedback presented and return with revisions at a future work session , along with an agenda item for potential approval at the same meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan , directing consultant to take feedback presented and return with revisions at a future work session , along with an agenda item for potential approval at the same meeting. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parks and trails master plan sent back for changes
motions.summary: The council delayed adopting the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan and sent it back to the consultant for revisions before a future work session.
motions.impact: No park or trail is affected yet. The plan meant to guide future park and trail decisions is still being reworked and returns to the council later.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City , Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15 regarding Noise to Modify Maximum Decibel Levels During Hours of Restriction as presented by staff , with the change that morning hours be adjusted from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., seven day a week
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City , Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15 regarding Noise to Modify Maximum Decibel Levels During Hours of Restriction as presented by staff , with the change that morning hours be adjusted from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., seven day a week. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Noise limits now lift at 7 a.m. instead of 9 a.m.
motions.summary: The city changed its noise rules, adjusting maximum decibel levels during restricted hours and moving the morning cutoff from 9 a.m. to 7 a.m., seven days a week.
motions.impact: This applies citywide, weekends included: the stricter noise limits now end at 7 a.m. rather than 9 a.m., so you may hear louder activity two hours earlier in the morning.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 2.35 (Public Library) and Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.15 (Roles and Duties) to Modify the Timing of Appointments from January 1 – December 31 to April 1 – March 31
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 2.35 (Public Library) and Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.15 (Roles and Duties) to Modify the Timing of Appointments from January 1 – December 31 to April 1 – March 31. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Board appointment terms shift to an April start
motions.summary: The city changed its code so library board and other appointments run April 1 through March 31 instead of the calendar year.
motions.impact: This touches people who serve on city boards, not the public. If you sit on one, your term now starts in April rather than January.

motions.item_title: Add pursuing a Justice Court with Utah County be added to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add pursuing a Justice Court with Utah County be added to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Justice court with Utah County added to priorities
motions.summary: The council added pursuing a justice court with Utah County to its Legislative Priorities List.
motions.impact: Nothing changes now, and no court is being created. This only flags the idea as something the city intends to pursue.

motions.item_title: Add a temporary business signage provision to the Legislative Priorities List, with direction f…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to add a temporary business signage provision to the Legislative Priorities List, with direction for staff to return with a proposal to the City Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Temporary business signs added to lobbying list
motions.summary: The council added a temporary business signage provision to its Legislative Priorities List and directed staff to come back with a proposal.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet for businesses or sign rules — this only puts the topic on the city's priority list and starts staff working on a proposal.
